question: What should init do when the host project is not a git repository: refuse, offer to run git init, or fall back to plain copies with no worktrees and a weaker rollback?

Plainer version of q16. Three things get counted in each agent's home: how often each note is looked up, how many friction entries pile up, and how often each rule fires. Per agent, as you said. The only open choice is storage. (A) One small file per home, say metrics.json, holding all three counts, updated by one shared script. (B) Each count stored where it arises: note counts inside the notes folder, friction counts derived from the history log on demand, rule firings in the router's firing log filtered by agent. A is one place to read and one writer to get right; B adds no new file but means three ways of reading. Which?
